chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fudayla ibn Ayoub, from Zurara, who said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'How should the man recite upon As-Safa and Al-Marwa?'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should say: There is no god except Allah, Alone, no partner for Him. For Him is the Kingdom and for Him is the Praise. He revives and causes to die, and He is Able over every thing.' Three times.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa, one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk during Sa'i
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwa, the second hill in the Sa'i ritual
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: La ilaha illa Allah, the declaration of monotheism
key_terms.لَهُ الْمُلْكُ: Lahu al-mulk, 'For Him is the Kingdom', an attribute of divine sovereignty
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ: Yuhyi wa yumit, 'He revives and causes to die', divine attributes

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended dhikr to recite while performing Sa'i between Safa and Marwa?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi prescribes a specific dhikr for the Sa'i ritual, emphasizing Allah's absolute sovereignty and power over life and death. The repetition of this declaration three times serves to reinforce the pilgrim's spiritual focus on divine unity (Tawhid) while traversing the symbolic hills, linking the physical act of worship with theological affirmation.
